name: Minimum Viable Experiment (MVE) Timeboxing
phase: Metrics, Telemetry, and Innovation Accounting Tactics
hypothesis: We believe we can determine whether to pursue [Hypothesis X] in five business days. We will verify this by running a structured, strictly timeboxed five-day testing sprint, and consider it validated if the team gathers enough behavioral data to pass an agreed quantitative validation gate by Day 5.
schematic: Timebox at step 1 of the 3-step strip

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: On Monday, isolate one critical unknown and design a test that can finish inside one week.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Build Monday and Tuesday, run live Wednesday and Thursday, close collection Friday at midday.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Present raw results Friday and force the decision: validate, invalidate or kill.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: On Monday morning, isolate a single critical unknown. Design an experiment whose asset preparation, user exposure, and data analysis can complete inside one business week.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Run asset preparation on Monday and Tuesday, deploy the test to live traffic on Wednesday and Thursday, and close data collection on Friday at midday.

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Present the raw results during a Friday retrospective, enforcing an immediate decision: Validate, Invalidate, or Kill.

warning.label: Sunk Cost Rationalization Extensions
warning.text: Teams extend a deadline when results look bad, hoping another few days salvages the hypothesis.

warningFull: Teams often extend testing deadlines when initial results are ambiguous or discouraging, hoping that running the test a few days longer will salvage their favored hypothesis.
